sentiment.instructions: Judge the overall sentiment the tweet's author expresses or conveys (their attitude, mood, or the emotional tone of the event described). Many tweets mention dates, events, or celebrities; label by the evaluative tone, not the topic.

criteria.positive: Author shows enthusiasm, excitement, liking, hope, gratitude, praise, or invites/promotes something in an upbeat way (come join, celebrate, free, win, get your tickets, don't miss, please share, come support). Also reported wins/achievements, condolences with prayers or blessings (RIP, may God bless), well-wishing. Cues: 'amazing', 'perfect', 'can't wait', 'love', 'favourite', 'lucky', 'thank you', 'hopefully', ':)'. Mild positive leaning counts.
criteria.neutral: Factual reports, bare schedules or dates without a call to action or upbeat wording, questions, requests, and remarks with no clear emotional slant. Also mixed or ambivalent feelings (envy of others going, mild reluctance, missing something for a reason), news-style sports/celebrity/political updates stated flatly. When positive and negative cues balance or the tone is light and observational, choose neutral.
criteria.negative: Author expresses anger, disgust, sadness, disappointment, dread, criticism, mockery, sarcasm, or insults (sucks, wtf, shit, hate, ugly, boring, going to die, ugh, :( ), sarcastic jabs at politicians, celebrities or institutions, or wishes harm. Also reports of violent, tragic or harmful events: attacks, bombings, deaths, crimes, arrests, disputes, economic losses, scandals, injuries.
